After months of Liquid Glass beta testing, WhatsApp is expanding the test scope of its new interface to include the iPad app, featuring a Mac-like sidebar. Here are the details.

WhatsApp is developing a brand-new iPad app layout

Although WhatsApp began adapting the Liquid Glass visual overhaul for the iOS app as early as last October, the company did not bring the new design to the iPad until June this year, in the form of a limited beta test.

At that time, WABetaInfo reported that the new design featured Liquid Glass-style tabs, buttons and context menus, while retaining the bottom tab bar used on the iPhone.

The website's latest report indicates that WhatsApp is rolling out another major interface change to some iPad users, replacing the existing bottom tab bar with a new Mac-like sidebar as the default interface.

This sidebar mimics the layout of the WhatsApp Mac version, allowing quick switching between "Chats", "Updates", "Communities", "Calls", Meta AI and other functional sections. Users can also hide the sidebar to free up more space for the chat list and conversation windows.

Below is the report:

WABetaInfo mentioned that some beta testers running the latest TestFlight version can already use the new sidebar, and some users using the regular App Store version have also begun to see this new interface.

As is WhatsApp's usual practice, the new interface will take some time to be rolled out to all users, regardless of whether they are using the beta or the official version. However, iPad users will eventually benefit from this more tablet-friendly layout.
